clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) gene
The classic triad is chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism and primary adrenal insufficiency
Diagnosis is usually made when two of the three classic components are present
It typically presents in childhood, often with candidiasis first, then hypoparathyroidism, then adrenal failure
Many other autoimmune features occur, including hypogonadism, type 1 diabetes, hepatitis, enamel and nail dystrophy and keratopathy
Lifelong surveillance is needed because components accrue over time; interferon-omega and anti-cytokine antibodies are characteristic markers
reference.pathophysiology: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 results from loss-of-function mutations in the AIRE gene, which normally drives expression of tissue-specific self-antigens in the thymus to delete autoreactive T cells. Defective AIRE function impairs central immune tolerance, allowing autoreactive lymphocytes to escape and attack multiple endocrine and non-endocrine tissues. The chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis reflects autoantibodies against T-helper-17 cytokines (such as IL-17 and IL-22), while organ-specific autoimmunity produces the endocrine failures and other manifestations.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated autoimmune Addison disease or hypoparathyroidism
additionalInvestigations: Assessment of the endocrine components (calcium, adrenal, gonadal, thyroid, glucose)
Ongoing periodic surveillance for evolving components
redFlags: Adrenal crisis from unrecognised adrenal insufficiency
reference.prognosis: The condition is lifelong with morbidity from cumulative organ involvement; with hormone replacement, antifungal treatment and vigilant monitoring, prognosis is much improved, though adrenal crisis and other complications remain risks.
pitfalls: Failing to anticipate additional components developing over time
Attributing candidiasis to simple immunodeficiency without recognising the syndrome
Overlooking the autosomal recessive inheritance and need for family evaluation
management: Hormone replacement for each failed gland: glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid for adrenal insufficiency, calcium with active vitamin D analogues for hypoparathyroidism, and levothyroxine and sex-hormone replacement as required
Antifungal therapy with azoles for chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, monitoring for resistance and oral carcinoma
Immunosuppression for non-endocrine autoimmune features such as autoimmune hepatitis
Adrenal crisis prevention with sick-day glucocorticoid rules and emergency parenteral hydrocortisone, commencing glucocorticoid before levothyroxine
Lifelong surveillance for cumulative endocrine and non-endocrine components that accrue over time
Genetic counselling and family testing; the condition is autosomal recessive due to AIRE mutations
